title: How to Add Google Analytics (GA4) to Carrd
summary: Carrd has no built-in visitor stats. To see who visits your site you add the GA4 tag through an Embed element, and Embeds need Pro Standard or higher.
steps: In Google Analytics, create a GA4 property and a Web data stream for your Carrd URL. Copy the full Google tag (the gtag.js snippet), not just the G- ID.
Open your site in the Carrd editor and click + (Add Element) → Embed.
Set Type to Code, Style to Hidden, and Location to Head.
Paste the full Google tag snippet into the Code box.
Publish the site, then open it in a new tab and check GA4 → Reports → Realtime. Your visit should show up within a minute.
gotchas: If Carrd won't let you add the Embed element, your plan doesn't include Embeds. Pro Lite does not have them.
Carrd sections load on the same page, so by default GA4 records one page view per visit. To track sections, turn on Enhanced Measurement → 'Page changes based on browser history events'.
Ad blockers hide 20–40% of visitors from GA4. Treat the numbers as a trend, not an exact count.
faq: Can I add Google Analytics to Carrd for free?
No. The free plan doesn't let you add custom code, and GA4 needs a code snippet. You need a plan that includes Embeds (Pro Standard or higher).
Where do I put the GA4 code in Carrd?
In a hidden Embed element with Location set to Head. That puts the tag in the page's <head>, which is where Google asks you to install it.
Does Carrd have its own analytics?
No. Carrd has no built-in analytics dashboard, so people use GA4 or a privacy-friendly tool like Plausible or Fathom, which go in through the same Embed element.

title: How to Connect a Custom Domain to Carrd
summary: Free Carrd sites live at yourname.carrd.co. To use yourname.com you need a Pro plan that includes custom domains, plus a domain you've bought from a registrar.
steps: Buy a domain from any registrar (Namecheap, Cloudflare, Porkbun, GoDaddy and so on).
In the Carrd editor, open the site menu → Publish settings, and change the domain option from the .carrd.co subdomain to Custom domain.
Enter your domain (for example example.com) and publish.
Carrd shows the DNS records to add. At your registrar, add exactly those records and remove any old A records for the same host.
Wait for DNS to update (usually minutes, sometimes a few hours), then load your domain. Carrd sets up HTTPS automatically once DNS resolves.
gotchas: Copy the DNS values from the Carrd screen itself. Carrd's IP addresses can change, so an old blog post may give you out-of-date values.
If you use Cloudflare, set the records to 'DNS only' (grey cloud) until Carrd has issued your certificate.
Decide on www or no www and set up the other one to redirect, so search engines don't index both.
faq: Can you use a custom domain on free Carrd?
No. Custom domains need a paid Pro plan that includes them. The free plan only publishes to a .carrd.co subdomain.
Does Carrd sell domains?
No. You buy the domain from a registrar and point it at Carrd with DNS records.
How long does a Carrd custom domain take to work?
Usually under an hour once the DNS records are right. It can take up to 24–48 hours if your registrar caches DNS for a long time.

title: How to Add a Contact Form to Carrd
summary: Carrd's Form element can send messages to your email or to tools like Mailchimp, but it's a paid feature. Here's how to set it up so messages don't end up in spam.
steps: Click + (Add Element) → Form.
Choose the Contact type (name, email, message) or Custom to pick your own fields.
Under the form's Send to setting, choose Email and enter the address that should receive messages.
Set a success action: show a message, or redirect to a thank-you section. A thank-you section also lets you track sign-ups as a GA4 event.
Publish, send yourself a test message, and check your spam folder the first time.
gotchas: The first few form emails often go to spam. Mark them 'Not spam' so later ones reach your inbox.
If the Form element is locked, your plan doesn't include forms.
To collect newsletter sign-ups rather than messages, use the Signup form type with a Mailchimp, ConvertKit or similar integration.
faq: Are Carrd forms free?
No. Forms are a Pro feature (Pro Standard and above). A free workaround is a mailto: button, but that shows your email address to spammers.
Can Carrd forms connect to Google Sheets?
Not directly. Send the form to a webhook (Zapier, Make or similar) and have that write a row to Google Sheets.
Where do Carrd form submissions go?
To whatever you pick under Send to: an email address, an email marketing tool, or a webhook URL.

title: How to Collect Email Sign-ups on Carrd (Mailchimp, ConvertKit and more)
summary: Many people use Carrd for waitlists and launch pages. A Signup form sends new subscribers straight to your email tool, with no Zapier needed for the main providers.
steps: Add Element → Form → Signup.
Under Send to, pick your provider (for example Mailchimp or ConvertKit) and connect it with the API key or list ID Carrd asks for.
Choose the list or audience that new sign-ups should join.
Keep it to one field (email) for the most sign-ups. Add a first-name field only if you'll really use it.
Publish and subscribe with a test address to check it arrives in your email tool.
gotchas: If your provider uses double opt-in, sign-ups only appear after they click the confirmation email.
If your provider isn't listed, use a webhook with Zapier or Make to connect it.
Put the form above the fold. On a one-page Carrd site, visitors decide within a few seconds.
faq: Can I make a waitlist page with Carrd?
Yes. A Carrd page with a Signup form is one of the fastest ways to build a waitlist. You need a Pro plan with forms.
Does Carrd integrate with Mailchimp?
Yes. Mailchimp is one of the providers built into the Signup form.

title: How to Remove 'Made with Carrd' Branding
summary: Free Carrd sites show a small 'Made with Carrd' badge. Any Pro plan removes it, and Pro Lite is the cheapest way to do that.
steps: Upgrade the account to any Pro plan.
Open the site in the editor. The branding option appears in the site/publish settings once you're on Pro.
Turn off the Carrd branding and publish again.
gotchas: Hiding the badge with CSS on the free plan needs custom code, which the free plan can't use, and it breaks Carrd's terms anyway.
If removing the badge is all you need, Pro Lite is enough. Pick a higher plan only if you also need forms, embeds or a custom domain.
faq: What is the cheapest Carrd plan without branding?
Pro Lite, the entry-level Pro plan.
Does removing Carrd branding help SEO?
Not directly. It mainly makes the site look more professional, which matters for portfolios and business pages.

title: How to Add a Spotify Player to Carrd
summary: Music carrds often show a Spotify song or playlist. The playable widget needs an Embed element (Pro Standard). On the free plan you can add a styled link button instead.
steps: In Spotify, open the song, album or playlist → ⋯ → Share → Embed track (or Embed playlist). Pick the compact or full size and copy the code.
In Carrd: Add Element → Embed. Set Type to Code and Style to Inline.
Paste the Spotify iframe code and set a width that fits your layout.
Publish and test on your phone, because Spotify's compact player behaves differently on mobile.
gotchas: Browsers won't autoplay music with sound, and Spotify's widget doesn't either. Visitors have to press play.
The free workaround is a Buttons element with a Spotify icon linking to the playlist. It's not playable on the page, but it takes up little space.
Apple Music has an embed tool too (on Apple's marketing tools site), and it goes in the same way.
faq: Can I add Spotify to Carrd for free?
You can link to Spotify for free. A playable embedded player needs the Embed element, which is Pro Standard or higher.
How do I add Apple Music to Carrd?
Get the embed code from Apple Music's share options or marketing tools, then paste it into an Embed element, the same way as Spotify.

title: How to Add Custom HTML, CSS & JavaScript to Carrd
summary: Almost every advanced Carrd trick (custom fonts, animations, widgets, tracking) runs through one element: Embed. Here's how it works and what it can do.
steps: Add Element → Embed.
Choose Type: Code for raw HTML/CSS/JS, or a URL-based type for supported widgets.
Choose Style: Inline shows the output where you place it. Hidden runs code without taking up space (for tracking, CSS and scripts).
For Hidden embeds, choose Location: Head for tracking tags and CSS, Body End for scripts that need the page to load first.
Publish. Embeds often don't run inside the editor preview, so always test on the live site.
gotchas: Write your CSS against your own element IDs (set in each element's settings). Carrd's generated class names can change.
Scripts that load before the page is ready will fail. Use Body End or wrap them in a DOMContentLoaded listener.
Heavy embeds slow down a one-page site. Keep third-party widgets to a minimum.
faq: Which Carrd plan allows custom code?
Embeds, and so custom code, need Pro Standard or higher.
Can I add custom CSS to Carrd?
Yes, with a hidden Embed element containing a <style> block, set to the Head location.

title: How to Add the Meta (Facebook) Pixel to Carrd
summary: If you run Instagram or Facebook ads to a Carrd landing page, you need the Meta Pixel to measure results. It installs through a hidden Embed.
steps: In Meta Events Manager, create a Pixel and copy its base code.
In Carrd: Add Element → Embed → Type: Code, Style: Hidden, Location: Head.
Paste the Pixel base code and publish.
Check it's working with the Meta Pixel Helper browser extension on your live URL.
To track sign-ups, send people to a thank-you section after the form and fire a Lead event there.
gotchas: iOS privacy settings and ad blockers hide many events. Use Meta's Conversions API if ad spend is significant.
If you serve visitors in the EU or UK, add a cookie consent step before the Pixel loads.
faq: Can I use the Facebook Pixel on free Carrd?
No. The Pixel needs custom code, and that needs an Embed-capable plan (Pro Standard or higher).

title: How to Password-Protect a Carrd Site
summary: Private portfolios, client previews and members-only pages need a password. Carrd offers this on its top plan, and the other routes are workarounds.
steps: Make sure the account is on the Pro tier that includes password protection (check Carrd's current plan comparison).
Open the site's publish/settings panel and turn on password protection.
Set the password, publish, and test in a private browser window.
gotchas: Hiding a section behind a secret #link isn't real protection. Anyone who finds the URL can see it.
Password-protected pages aren't indexed by search engines, so don't protect a page you want to rank.
faq: Can you password protect Carrd for free?
No. Real password protection is a paid feature on Carrd's higher tier.

title: How to Sell Products or Take Payments on Carrd
summary: Carrd isn't a store, but one-product pages, commissions, digital downloads and pre-orders work well. Use payment links, or a payment-enabled form where your plan includes one.
steps: Easiest route: create a Stripe Payment Link, PayPal.me link, Ko-fi or Gumroad product for each item.
In Carrd, add a Buttons element (the 'Buy' button) that links to that payment link. Buttons work on every plan.
For custom fields such as commission details, use a Form element and send people to the payment link after they submit.
Add a thank-you/confirmation section and set the payment link's success URL to it, so you can track purchases.
gotchas: Payment links send buyers off your site to pay, which is normal and trusted for small sellers.
Artists taking commissions: say your terms of service and refund policy on the page before the Buy button.
faq: Can you sell on Carrd?
Yes, for a small number of products. Link Buy buttons to Stripe, PayPal, Ko-fi or Gumroad. For a full catalogue, use a real e-commerce platform.
Is Carrd good for art commissions?
Yes, it's one of the most popular uses. Put a price sheet, TOS and a request form (Pro) or a Ko-fi link (free) on one page.

title: How to Make a Multi-Page Site in Carrd
summary: Carrd is built around one page, but hidden sections work like separate pages: /#about, /#work, /#contact. Here's how to set up navigation that feels like a multi-page site.
steps: Add Element → Section break (a Header/Footer or Section divider). Each section break starts a new 'page'.
Give each section a name, such as about. Its URL becomes yoursite.com/#about.
Make a nav with a Buttons or Links element pointing to #about, #work, #contact.
Set the first section as the default (home) and hide the others until their link is clicked.
Use the Header/Footer section setting for navigation that appears on every 'page'.
gotchas: Search engines treat all sections as one URL. If you want each topic to rank on its own, build separate sites (Pro plans allow several) or use a multi-page builder.
Element limits apply to the whole site, so very large sites can hit them.
faq: Can Carrd have multiple pages?
Carrd sites are one page, but hidden sections with their own #links act like pages. Pro plans also let you build several separate sites.
Does each Carrd section get indexed separately by Google?
No. #section URLs are treated as the same page.
